{"grammar":"Compose ONE canvas card as OpenUI Lang for Acute-Notes. The card's Markdown is its text; this layout is how it is drawn.

## Syntax Rules

1. Each statement is on its own line: `identifier = Expression`
2. `root` is the entry point — every program must define `root = IdeaCard(...)`
3. Expressions are: strings ("..."), numbers, booleans (true/false), null, arrays ([...]), objects ({...}), or component calls TypeName(arg1, arg2, ...)
4. Use references for readability: define `name = ...` on one line, then use `name` later
5. EVERY variable (except root) MUST be referenced by at least one other variable. Unreferenced variables are silently dropped and will NOT render. Always include defined variables in their parent's children/items array.
6. Arguments are POSITIONAL (order matters, not names). Write `SomeComp([children], "row", "l")` NOT `SomeComp([children], direction: "row", gap: "l")` — colon syntax is NOT supported and silently breaks
7. Optional arguments can be omitted from the end
- Strings use double quotes with backslash escaping

## Component Signatures

Arguments marked with ? are optional. Sub-components can be inline or referenced; prefer references for better streaming.
Props marked `$binding<type>` accept a `$variable` reference for two-way binding.

CitationChip(unit: string, label?: string) — An inline marker citing one source unit this card represents. Use one per unit cited, never one chip for several units.
SourceLink(unit: string, label?: string) — A prominent 'view in source' affordance for one unit, distinct from an inline CitationChip.
Callout(tone: "info" | "warning" | "success", text: string) — A short aside flagging something about the idea itself (a caveat, an open question, why it needs review) — not a citation and not the idea's main body.
ComparisonTable(columns: string[], rows: string[][]) — A small table for comparing a few options or facts side by side. Keep it to a handful of rows; prose fits better in the card body otherwise.
IdeaCard(title: string, body: string, importance?: "low" | "medium" | "high", citations?: CitationChip[], detail?: string, extras?: (Callout | ComparisonTable | SourceLink | NoteLink)[]) — The root of one distilled idea card: a title, the idea in the model's own words, how important it is, and the source units it represents. Optional `detail` is a longer explanation shown only when the reader asks for more; optional `extras` holds at most a couple of Callout/ComparisonTable/SourceLink/NoteLink children when truly needed — most cards are just title + body + citations.
DecisionOption(name: string, pros?: string[], cons?: string[]) — One option a DecisionCard weighs: its name and short pros/cons. Only used inside DecisionCard.options.
DecisionCard(question: string, options: DecisionOption[], chosen?: string, rationale?: string, citations?: string[]) — A decision and the options weighed for it. `options` are DecisionOption children; `chosen` is the exact name of the option decided on (omit if undecided); `rationale` says why; `citations` are source unit ids.
TimelineEvent(when: string, label: string, detail?: string, unit?: string) — One dated event in a Timeline: when, a short label, optional detail, optional source unit id. Only used inside Timeline.events.
Timeline(title: string, events: TimelineEvent[]) — Events in time order (TimelineEvent children). Use for history, rollouts, incident sequences — not for unordered facts.
FlowDiagram(title: string, steps: string[], details?: string[], citations?: string[]) — A short process as connected steps, left to right. `details[i]` explains step i and shows when the reader selects it. Keep to 2–7 steps. `citations` are source unit ids.
QuizCard(question: string, choices: string[], answer: number, explanation?: string, unit?: string, selected?: $binding<number>) — A multiple-choice check on one idea. `answer` is the 0-based index of the correct choice; `explanation` is shown after answering; `unit` is the source unit it tests. `selected` may be bound to a $variable to share the pick.
Flashcard(front: string, back: string, unit?: string) — A study card: `front` is a prompt (usually the idea's title), `back` the idea itself; the reader flips it. `unit` is the source unit.
NoteLink(target: string, label?: string) — A link to another note in the same notes view, by its note id. Use for 'see also' between related ideas; never invent an id.

## Hoisting & Streaming (CRITICAL)

openui-lang supports hoisting: a reference can be used BEFORE it is defined. The parser resolves all references after the full input is parsed.

During streaming, the output is re-parsed on every chunk. Undefined references are temporarily unresolved and appear once their definitions stream in. This creates a progressive top-down reveal — structure first, then data fills in.

**Recommended statement order for optimal streaming:**
1. `root = IdeaCard(...)` — UI shell appears immediately
2. Component definitions — fill in as they stream
3. Data values — leaf content last

Always write the root = IdeaCard(...) statement first so the UI shell appears immediately, even before child data has streamed in.
## Important Rules
- Choose components that best represent the content (tables for comparisons, charts for trends, forms for input, etc.)

## Final Verification
Before finishing, walk your output and verify:
1. root = IdeaCard(...) is the FIRST line (for optimal streaming).
2. Every referenced name is defined. Every defined name (other than root) is reachable from root.

- A layout is how the card is DRAWN; its Markdown stays the card's text (search, export and study read the Markdown). Write the Markdown first, then a layout that shows the same facts.
- `root` may be any component above, not only IdeaCard.
- Static only: the only calls are the components above. No Query, Mutation, Action, OpenUrl, builtin functions or $state — they are refused.
- Every number the layout shows must appear in the card's Markdown or in a passage it cites; a new number is refused.
- Cite passages only with `sourceId` (one of the open canvas's content sources) and that source's unit ids, e.g. CitationChip("u3"); an id the source doesn't have is refused.
- A phrase mostly in words the Markdown doesn't use is accepted but flagged to the user in the review.
- Limits: 16000 characters of Lang, 120 statements, 200 components, 8000 characters of visible text.
- Passing these checks means nothing mechanical was found — not that the layout is right. Every layout waits for the user's review; nothing changes until they accept.

## Examples

### IdeaCard — one idea with its sources (the default)

root = IdeaCard("Retry policy", "Jobs retry 5 times, then give up.", "high", [c1])
c1 = CitationChip("u3")

### Timeline — dated or ordered events

root = Timeline("Release", [e1, e2])
e1 = TimelineEvent("Monday", "Build")
e2 = TimelineEvent("Tuesday", "Deploy", "Only after QA sign-off")

### FlowDiagram — steps in order

root = FlowDiagram("Release pipeline", ["Build", "QA sign-off", "Deploy"], ["CI builds and tests", "A QA engineer signs off", "The release manager deploys"])

### DecisionCard — a question, its options and the choice

root = DecisionCard("Which database?", [o1, o2], "Postgres", "The team already runs it.")
o1 = DecisionOption("Postgres", ["Team knows it"], ["Needs tuning"])
o2 = DecisionOption("MySQL")

### ComparisonTable — a few entities by the same attributes
